question: To determine the actual values of embedded emissions under CBAM, verification by an accredited verifier is required. If these values cannot be verified, companies must rely on default values for the relevant types of goods. These are often significantly higher than the actual values (100 % to 600 % higher).

However, the accreditation timeline for potential verifiers is ambitious and it remains unclear to them what requirements need to be meet. As a result, there are as of yet no accredited verifiers, which in turn leads to uncertainty among CBAM declarants. 1.

Does the Commission share the view that a shortage of verifiers has disproportionate consequences for authorised CBAM declarants, and how long does it expect it will take to bring the number of accredited verifiers up to the required level?
How is the Commission encouraging the registration of new accredited verifiers, and what additional measures is it taking to address this issue?

Does the Commission agree that companies which have completed all the necessary steps should not be penalised by a lack of accredited verifiers, and is it prepared to apply a more flexible default value if such companies are unable to find an accredited verifier?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.7.2026) The Commission adopted the implementing rules on the calculation of embedded emissions as well as on their verification and the accreditation of verifiers in end-2025. In accordance with Regulation (EU) 2023/956, Member States’ national accreditation bodies need to accredit legal persons to be Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) verifiers.

The Commission is in regular contact with national accreditation bodies (NABs) as well as with the European cooperation for Accreditation (EA). 20 NABs have already indicated that they would provide CBAM accreditation services and some have opened applications for verifiers that are already accredited under the EU Emission Trading System in April 2026.

The Commission is organising webinars as well as preparing a guidance document and a survey for interested applicants. Enabling authorised CBAM declarants to declare embedded emissions also on the basis of actual values – and not only on default values – is a priority of the Commission and it will follow the matter closely.

It is important to ensure that there will be sufficient verification capacity in time for the submission of the first CBAM declarations by 30 September 2027. Importers of CBAM goods should ensure that third-country suppliers monitor and calculate embedded emissions in accordance with the CBAM Regulation. The mark-up on the default values is gradually phased in, from 2026 onwards.
This applies for all the CBAM sectors except the fertilisers, for which the mark-up is kept lower, at 1%.
